title: cache-hf composite (.github/actions/cache-hf): only the job that populates a cache key gets cache-mode write; restore-only consumers get read
answers: Windows slow tests keep re-downloading Hugging Face datasets on every run
Which CI jobs are allowed to save the Hugging Face datasets cache?
Can I still pass restore-only to the cache-hf action?
Where is the Hugging Face datasets cache handled in CI?
body:
Path: .github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml caches ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/datasets-- with a key of runner.os plus the hash of tests/data/test_huggingface_dataset_and_source.py; it is called by test workflows such as master.yml, slow-tests.yml, protobuf-cross-test.yml and test-requirements.yml.
Rule: The composite has no restore-only input and always runs actions/cache. Control saves per job instead: the job that writes a key gets `cache-mode: write` (master.yml writes the Linux key, the slow-tests.yml windows job writes the Windows key), and jobs that only restore get `cache-mode: read` with no restore-only input. Choose writer or reader by the key the job computes and by whether it runs on schedule or dispatch, not by whether it is a pull request job.
Symptom: Marking the Windows slow-tests job read-only left the Windows HF cache key with no writer, so after a miss every run would redownload the datasets; review caught it and the job was set to write.
Constraints: The key includes runner.os, so each OS has its own key and needs its own writer. Read-only jobs must not be the only job for a key. Scheduled and manual runs still save, so they need write when they are the populator.
applies: Changes to the cache-hf composite action or to which CI jobs read or write the HF datasets cache.
says: Windows slow test runs keep downloading Hugging Face datasets from scratch every time.
Ensure Windows continuous integration builds save their downloaded dataset cache for future runs.
Automated test jobs on Windows are taking too long because cache misses persist.
Configure dataset cache permissions so only populating pipeline jobs can save cached files.
search: In .github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml, jobs that populate the Hugging Face dataset cache key must use cache-mode: write, while restore-only consumers use cache-mode: read without a restore-only input. Because cache keys incorporate runner.os alongside the hash of tests/data/test_huggingface_dataset_and_source.py, each operating system requires an assigned writer job, such as master.yml for Linux and slow-tests.yml for Windows. Writer status must be determined by the computed cache key and whether the job runs on schedule or dispatch rather than pull request status.
